analysis_summary.scope: Validated Phase 1 IR and Semgrep candidates directly against Kubio 2.7.1 source, prioritizing REST/AJAX/import/file-operation paths and contributor-or-lower reachable surfaces.
highlights: No Patchstack-eligible true positive was confirmed from the reviewed candidates.
Most REST exposure alerts were false positives because the live routes enforce permission callbacks such as current_user_can('edit_theme_options') or controller permission methods.
Two flows remain REVIEW: one multisite-oriented file-read-to-cloud-upload path in /snippet, and one demo-site plugin install/activate capability mismatch that depends on deployment role semantics.

findings.vuln_type: Path Traversal to Arbitrary File Read with Second-Order Cloud Exfiltration
findings.auth_required: authenticated user with edit_theme_options; most relevant on multisite site-admin contexts

reasoning.hypothesis: The /snippet REST route accepts attacker-controlled snippet JSON and may treat forged upload URLs as local filesystem paths without constraining them to the uploads directory.
trace: The route /snippet is registered with permission_callback current_user_can('edit_theme_options') at plugins/kubio/lib/api/colibri.php:48-57.

kubio_save_block_snippet reads the untrusted request parameter snippet via get_param('snippet') at plugins/kubio/lib/api/colibri.php:112 and passes it into kubio_create_snippet_zip at plugins/kubio/lib/api/colibri.php:129.

kubio_create_snippet_zip regex-parses every URL under wp_get_upload_dir()['baseurl'] from the JSON-encoded snippet at plugins/kubio/lib/api/colibri.php:263-267, concatenates each captured suffix directly onto wp_get_upload_dir()['basedir'] at plugins/kubio/lib/api/colibri.php:278-279, and reads the resolved path with file_get_contents at plugins/kubio/lib/api/colibri.php:281-284.
After zipping the gathered files, kubio_save_block_snippet uploads the archive body to the snippets cloud endpoint at plugins/kubio/lib/api/colibri.php:133-151.

The same edit_theme_options role can also set kubio_cloud_api_key through /kubio-api-key at plugins/kubio/lib/api/kubio-cloud.php:23-32 and plugins/kubio/lib/api/kubio-cloud.php:86-90, so the upload credential is user-controllable in the same trust boundary.
defenses: The destination host is fixed to Kubio cloud via KUBIO_CLOUD_URL and Utils::getSnippetsURL() at plugins/kubio/plugin.php:67-68 and plugins/kubio/lib/src/Core/Utils.php:477-485.
The route is not public; it requires edit_theme_options.
refutation: I did not find any realpath, basename, validate_file, or prefix check that rejects .. segments before file_exists/file_get_contents is reached.
The fixed host refutes generic SSRF, but it does not refute local file disclosure into the ZIP payload if an attacker-controlled or attacker-chosen kubio_cloud_api_key is accepted.

What remains unproven from source alone is whether the cloud service will always accept an attacker-controlled API key and whether the uploaded ZIP can be retrieved by that same account without dynamic verification.
reasoning.conclusion: The local source-to-sink traversal is real in code, and the same capability boundary can set the cloud API key used for upload. Because end-to-end attacker retrieval depends on external Kubio cloud behavior not visible in this repository, I am keeping this as REVIEW instead of TP.

findings.poc_description: In a multisite test where a site admin has edit_theme_options, first POST /wp-json/kubio/v1/kubio-api-key with an attacker-controlled Kubio cloud API key. Then POST /wp-json/kubio/v1/snippet with snippet JSON containing a forged URL such as https://target.example/wp-content/uploads/../../wp-config.php. The code path at kubio_create_snippet_zip will resolve the traversal path, read it into the ZIP, and send that ZIP to the snippets cloud endpoint using kubio_cloud_api_key.
findings.remediation: Resolve candidate asset paths with realpath(), reject any path containing traversal, and enforce that the normalized path stays under wp_get_upload_dir()['basedir']. Prefer attachment-ID based resolution over raw URL scraping. If snippet uploads can move server-side file data off host, gate both /snippet and /kubio-api-key behind a stronger capability on multisite.

findings.vuln_type: Insufficient Capability Check for Plugin Installation/Activation
findings.auth_required: authenticated user who can satisfy current_user_can('import') and obtain the demo-site nonce

reasoning.hypothesis: The demo-site AJAX flow allows plugin install/activation after only checking the import capability, not install_plugins/activate_plugins, which may be too weak on some deployments such as multisite.
trace: DemoSites registers wp_ajax_kubio-demo-site-install-plugin and wp_ajax_kubio-demo-site-activate-plugin at plugins/kubio/lib/src/DemoSites/DemoSites.php:323-324.
Both handlers call DemoSitesHelpers::verifyAjaxCall() first at plugins/kubio/lib/src/DemoSites/DemoSites.php:327-328 and plugins/kubio/lib/src/DemoSites/DemoSites.php:347-348.
verifyAjaxCall only checks the kubio-ajax-demo-site-verification nonce and current_user_can('import') at plugins/kubio/lib/src/DemoSites/DemoSitesHelpers.php:15-19.

The install handler then reads $_REQUEST['slug'] at plugins/kubio/lib/src/DemoSites/DemoSites.php:331 and passes it to PluginsManager::installPlugin at plugins/kubio/lib/src/DemoSites/DemoSites.php:337, which reaches Plugin_Upgrader->install(...) at plugins/kubio/lib/src/PluginsManager.php:48-65 without any local install_plugins check.

The sibling activate handler reads $_REQUEST['slug'] at plugins/kubio/lib/src/DemoSites/DemoSites.php:351 and reaches activate_plugin(...) at plugins/kubio/lib/src/PluginsManager.php:98-105, again without any local activate_plugins check.
The nonce is emitted into the starter-sites UI and inline editor data at plugins/kubio/lib/admin-pages/main-page/demo-sites.php:198-202 and plugins/kubio/lib/editor-assets.php:374-380.
refutation: I did not find any Kubio-side current_user_can('install_plugins') or current_user_can('activate_plugins') check in this flow.

I also did not find Kubio code that grants import to low roles during the normal web flow; the allowImportCaps helper is only wired in CLI-specific paths at plugins/kubio/lib/filters/wp-import.php:202-204 and plugins/kubio/lib/src/Core/Activation.php:50-52.

The unresolved point is WordPress deployment semantics: if only full administrators satisfy import on the affected site, then the issue becomes admin-only; if a lower privileged actor such as a multisite site admin can satisfy import while lacking install/activate plugin privileges, the flow becomes a real privilege boundary break.
reasoning.conclusion: The capability mismatch is real in Kubio code, but I cannot prove from this repository alone that a Patchstack-relevant non-admin actor reaches current_user_can('import') on the target deployment. Keep as REVIEW, with multisite/site-admin validation prioritized.

findings.poc_description: On a deployment where a non-super-admin role passes current_user_can('import'), obtain the kubio-ajax-demo-site-verification nonce from the starter-sites UI or localized editor data, then POST to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php with action=kubio-demo-site-install-plugin, slug=<wordpress-org-plugin>, nonce=<nonce>. Follow with action=kubio-demo-site-activate-plugin and the same slug to test whether Kubio bypasses the normal install_plugins/activate_plugins boundary.
findings.remediation: Require current_user_can('install_plugins') in installPlugin() and current_user_can('activate_plugins') in activatePlugin(), in addition to the existing nonce. On multisite, explicitly honor the network/site distinction before calling Plugin_Upgrader or activate_plugin.

negative_findings.summary: Menu REST routes are not public despite Phase 1 / Semgrep missing-permission signals.
negative_findings.reasoning: Both controllers attach permission callbacks before read or write actions. The menu controller uses get_permissions() -> current_user_can('edit_theme_options'), and the menu-locations controller uses explicit permission-check methods that return WP_Error unless edit_theme_options is present.

negative_findings.summary: The get-started tab include is not a raw user-controlled LFI.
negative_findings.reasoning: The request only provides a sanitized tab key via sanitize_key($_REQUEST['tab']). Kubio then looks up that key in kubio_get_started_page_tabs() and uses the mapped tab-partial value. The request does not flow directly into require_once; exploitation would require a trusted filter to inject a malicious tab definition first.

negative_findings.summary: Contact-form and newsletter shortcode XSS candidates are neutralized by kses/context escaping before output.
negative_findings.reasoning: The contact-form shortcode runs wp_kses_post() on the embedded shortcode string before do_shortcode(), and the newsletter renderer escapes labels/placeholders with esc_html/esc_attr while wrapping rich label text in wp_kses_post(). I did not find an unescaped attribute/body sink reachable directly from shortcode attributes.

negative_findings.summary: The Image Hub plugin installer is capability-gated correctly.
negative_findings.reasoning: The AJAX handler verifies the kubio_ajax_nonce and immediately enforces current_user_can('install_plugins') before invoking PluginsManager::installPlugin() or activatePlugin().

negative_findings.summary: Preview changeset deletion enforces both nonce validation and ownership.
negative_findings.reasoning: kubio-delete-changeset requires a valid kubio_ajax_nonce, resolves the changeset by UUID, and only deletes when the changeset post_author matches get_current_user_id(). I did not find cross-user deletion.

negative_findings.summary: Most high-value REST mutation surfaces flagged in Phase 1 are admin-gated in live code.
negative_findings.reasoning: The reviewed AI, settings, entity-save, and third-party theme import routes consistently enforce current_user_can('edit_theme_options') in permission_callback, so the IR 'unknown auth' labeling overstated their exposure.

out_of_scope.auth_required: authenticated user who can reach the hidden get-started page and obtain a kubio_clear_ai_logs nonce
out_of_scope.reasoning: The action deletes files returned by FileLog::get_log_files('AI') and is only surfaced when KUBIO_AI_LOG is enabled. This is a developer-log integrity issue, but I did not find privilege escalation, code execution, or sensitive data exposure with practical Patchstack impact.

out_of_scope.vuln_type: Notice/transient state manipulation without material security impact
out_of_scope.auth_required: authenticated user with the corresponding admin-page nonce
out_of_scope.reasoning: The dismissable-notice handler only updates the _kubio_dismissable_notices option's dismiss_time, and the remote-notifications AJAX only refreshes a cached transient from Kubio's fixed notification endpoint. Per Patchstack rules, notice-only or similarly low-grade state changes are not meaningful enough to keep as actionable findings.
